haiku-low.q1: They see the generic reply: "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is written and no email is sent.
haiku-low.q2: Nothing is written and no email is sent, but the user sees the same generic reply as every other request.
haiku-low.q3: It works for 30 minutes from issue and only once. It ends sooner if it is used or if a newer link is issued for the account, which revokes it.
haiku-low.q4: The link stays valid and unused, since a rejected password does not use up the link. It remains usable until it expires.
haiku-low.q5: No devices stay logged in, because all sessions for the account are deleted, including the one that made the reset. The user must go to the login page and log in again.
haiku-low.q6: The worker retries 3 times with growing delays, then logs the failure and drops the job. Nobody is alerted and the user is not told.
haiku-low.q7: The raw token is placed in the email job's link when the link is issued. The worker then sends that email through the mail provider. Only the hash is stored in the database.
haiku-low.q8: The server computes SHA-256 of the token from the link and looks up the reset_tokens row with that hash. It checks that used_at and revoked_at are empty and expires_at is in the future.
haiku-low.q9: It is not stored separately; it is counted from reset_tokens rows created for the user in the last hour. Rows drop out as they age past one hour, and revoked rows still count.
haiku-low.q10: Earlier unused links for the account are marked revoked in the same transaction as the insert of the new link, so two links never work at once.
haiku-low.q11: The new password hash is saved, the token is marked used, and sessions are deleted, all in one transaction with the confirmation email job. The email is queued in that same transaction, not afterwards.
haiku-low.q12: Marking the token used is one conditional update that succeeds only if it is still unused, unrevoked and unexpired. Only one submit changes the row; the other changes 0 rows and is rejected.

sonnet.q1: They see the generic reply: "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is written and no email is sent.
sonnet.q2: The limit is 3 links per account per rolling hour, so the server stops. It writes nothing and sends nothing, and still shows the generic reply.
sonnet.q3: A link works for 30 minutes from issue and can be used once. It ends sooner if it is used, or if a newer link is issued, which marks it revoked.
sonnet.q4: The link is not used up. Nothing is saved, and it stays valid until it expires. The user sees the form again with an error.
sonnet.q5: None. All of the user's sessions are deleted, including the device that made the reset. The user is redirected to the login page and logs in again, because there is no automatic login.
sonnet.q6: The worker retries up to 3 times with growing delays, then logs the failure and drops the job. Nobody is told or alerted, and the user gets no email. The link stays valid, and each new request counts toward the hourly limit.
sonnet.q7: In Flow 1 the API makes the 32 random raw bytes and stores only the SHA-256 hash in the database. It puts the raw token into the link inside the email job that it adds to the queue. The worker then sends that email.
sonnet.q8: The server takes the token from the link and computes SHA-256(token). It looks for a reset_tokens row with that hash where used_at and revoked_at are empty and expires_at is in the future. If a row is found, it shows the new-password form with the raw token in a hidden field. If not, it shows the expired page.
sonnet.q9: The count comes from the reset_tokens table: it counts that user's rows created in the last hour, and revoked rows still count. It is a rolling hour, so rows drop out of the count once they are more than an hour old. There is no fixed reset.
sonnet.q10: The earlier unused links for that account are marked revoked (revoked_at). This happens in the same transaction as the insert of the new row, so two links never work at once.
sonnet.q11: All in one transaction: the token is marked used, the new password hash is saved, all of the user's sessions are deleted, and the "password changed" email job is added to the queue. The job is queued as part of that same transaction, so either all of it happens or none of it does.
sonnet.q12: Step C1 is one conditional update that marks the token used only if it is still unused, not revoked and not expired. Only one submit can change the row (1 row). The other changes 0 rows, so its transaction stops and it gets the expired page.
